simple.meaning: אַזְכָּרָה (ʼazkârâh) is a Hebrew concept word meaning “a reminder ; specifically remembrance-offering.” BibleIQ follows how Scripture develops this idea across its occurrences.
simple.biblicalBackground: The concept appears 7 times across Leviticus, Numbers, beginning at Leviticus 2:2. Its contexts include family line, offering, altar, priesthood.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to אַזְכָּרָה (H234).
simple.whyItMatters: Concept words shape biblical themes. BibleIQ keeps the concept grounded in actual verse evidence instead of starting with a later theological definition.
simple.summary: אַזְכָּרָה (ʼazkârâh) / H234 is traced through Leviticus 2:2, Leviticus 2:9, Leviticus 2:16, Leviticus 5:12 as a generated source-based concept entry.

firstOccurrence.englishText: He shall bring it to Aaron’s sons, the priests. He shall take his handful of its fine flour, and of its oil, with all its frankincense, and the priest shall burn its memorial on the altar, an offering made by fire, of a pleasant aroma to Yahweh.

definitions.full: H234. azkarah אַזְכָּרָה noun feminine memorial-offering , only P (an Aramaic infinitive form; compare Ba NB 90 Sta § 224 ) — absolute ׳א Lev 24:7 ; suffix אַזְכָּֽרָתָהּ 2:2 5 t.; — used of the frankincense burned for the shew-bread לאז ׳ללחם לי ׳אִשֶּׁה והיתה 24:7 ; elsewhere always after הקטיר , only with suffix, referring to מִנְחָה 2:2 , 9 , 16 ; 6:8 ; Num 5:26 ; of the meal used as חַטָּאת by the very poor Lev 5:12 ; always connected with אִשֶּׁה , except 6:8 ; Num 5:26 .
